Find ONE real, bounded defect in it: an input on which a public function returns a wrong result, raises an unexpected exception, or violates its own docstring/contract. You may NOT change command-center/bcc/features/economy_swarm.py; do NOT fix anything. Reproduce the defect by adding ONE new test function at the end of command-center/tests/test_economy_swarm.py that FAILS on the current code because of the defect and would pass once it is fixed. The test must call the module's public API, must not use network, wall-clock time, randomness or machine specifics, and its expected value must follow from the module's docstring, names or established behaviour, not from taste. Run command-center/tests/test_economy_swarm.py with run_tests: your new test must fail for the reason you describe, every other test in the file must still pass. If you find no real defect, change nothing and answer NO_DEFECT. Final answer in this form: DEFECT: <function> | INPUT: <...> | EXPECTED: <...> | ACTUAL: <...> | TEST: <test function name>.

     assert allowed_actions(already_used) == ("stop_blocked",)
+

+def test_ling_pass_does_not_offer_ling_repair_when_blockers_present():
+    # When Ling verification passes, we should not offer a Ling repair attempt,
+    # because there is nothing to repair. The Ling repair action is defined as
+    # "Give the free Ling coder one bounded repair attempt, then verify again."
+    # It only makes sense when verification has not passed or after a previous
+    # repair attempt. The paid_eligible function also treats Ling PASS as a
+    # condition that does not require paid GLM, implying Ling PASS satisfies
+    # the verification goal.
+    req = RouteIn(
+        stage="repair",
+        ling_attempts=1,
+        ling_verdict="PASS",
+        unresolved_blockers=1,  # blockers present but Ling passed
+        allow_paid=True,
+        paid_budget_usd=0.25,
+    )
+    allowed = allowed_actions(req)
+    # Ling repair should not be offered when verification passed.
+    assert "ling_repair" not in allowed
+    # Instead, we expect only stop_blocked (and possibly aster_audit? but aster_audit
+    # is only offered when unresolved_blockers == 0 per the code).
+    # The current code returns ling_repair and stop_blocked, so this test will
+    # fail until the code is fixed to not include ling_repair.
